gateIssues.message: KILLER GRAMMAR_ERROR rejected: the answer is a shallow subject-verb number flip ("were" ↔ "was") with the true subject sitting right next to the verb (no genuine attractor noun in between). At KILLER the agreement must span a real long-distance modifier with a misleading attractor noun so the subject head is non-obvious. Move the error to such a site, or pick another deep structure already in the passage: a long-distance subject-verb agreement across a genuine intervening relative/appositive or of/with phrase, a nominal vs relative clause-gap, a participle voice error, or a parallel-structure break.

KILLER GRAMMAR_ERROR answer is tagged with generic pointCode (a); use a precise structural frame such as agreement with modifier, participle clause, relative/nominal clause, voice, complement, dummy it, inversion, or nonfinite pattern.

The error mutation "learning" → "learn" sits after the perception/help verb "seen" with an object in between — the mutated bare form re-parses as a valid perception-verb complement, so it is still grammatical; the item has no single wrong answer.
Underline (C) is tagged pointCode (k) but its surface "learn" has no token matching that grammar point — the label looks fabricated. Move the underline onto the real k-token or fix the code.
